newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland Elec hopes for efficiency benefits.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland Elec hopes for efficiency benefits.

text.p: British regional electricity company Northern Ireland Electricity said on Thursday that it expected a re-focusing of its business would deliver efficiencies to benefit customers and shareholders.

In a statement with half year results, the company said that a current review of its pricing being considered by the UK's Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) would "have an impact on our future income," however.
The company said pretax profits for the half year rose to 52 million stg from 47.7 million stg previously and paid an interim dividend of 5.5 pence per share, up from five pence previously.
The MMC is due to report on a pricing dispute between Northern Ireland Electricity and its regulator Ofreg by March 17.

"We are an isolated system and cannot be expected to achieve similar tariffs to the UK companies which have the benefits of economy of scale and diversification of generation source," the company said.
The company said that electricity sales "continue to reflect good economic performance in the region."
